takeaway: Tibialis anterior and posterior together invert the foot; the peronei evert it.

question.text: Which of the following muscles act together to invert the foot?

lines.text: Think of the foot as a car, and inversion as steering its sole inward, at the subtalar joint.
Two twins both wearing Tib caps are doing the steering: tibialis anterior and tibialis posterior.
Working alone, tibialis anterior dorsiflexes the foot, and tibialis posterior plantarflexes it.
Together, those opposite pulls cancel out, leaving pure inversion.
Tibialis anterior is supplied by the deep peroneal nerve, and tibialis posterior by the tibial nerve.
On the other side, the peroneus brothers pull the sole outward, which is eversion.
So the pair that inverts the foot is tibialis anterior and tibialis posterior.
